title: Intestinal organoid co-culture protocol to study cell competition in vitro
protocol: Pre-warm 24-well culture plates at least 1 day prior to co-culture initiation.
Check well confluency and organoid condition under the microscope.
Select wells with similar organoid density as estimated by eye for a 1:1 ratio co-culture.
Alternatively, count the amount of organoids per well manually or using ImageJ.
Remove ENR medium from the wells containing organoids.
Add 250 μL Cell Recovery Solution to 50 μL Matrigel domes.
Pipette up and down using a P1000 filter tip to disrupt the Matrigel.
Transfer the organoid solution of both populations into a sterile 15 mL tube.
Mix thoroughly by pipetting up and down to break down organoid fragments.
Incubate on ice for 30 minutes.
Centrifuge the tube at 480×g for 4 minutes.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the organoid pellet in an appropriate volume of Matrigel.
Add approximately 80 μl Matrigel per well for a 24-well plate, including an extra 30 μl.
Keep the Matrigel ice-cold during handling.
Pipette up and down to mix organoid populations before plating.
Plate exactly 50 μl of Matrigel containing co-culture suspension per well of a pre-warmed 24-well plate.
Transfer the culture plate to an incubator (37°C, 5% CO2) for approximately 15 min.
Turn the plate upside down after about 5 minutes.
Provide each well with 500 μl of pre-warmed ENR culture medium.
Mechanically disrupt organoids.
Mix suspensions in Eppendorf vials.
Mildly centrifuge and resuspend the cell pellet in a small volume of ENR medium.
Incubate the organoid mixtures at 37°C for 30 min to ensure cell fragments stick together.
Centrifuge the organoid mixture at 480×g for 4 min.
Discard the supernatant.
Plate the organoids in Matrigel domes.
Calculate the volume of Collagen I and neutralization buffer needed for a final concentration of 1mg/mL in 1 mL.
Gently mix the calculated volume of Collagen I and neutralization buffer.
Pipette 1 mL of the mixed Collagen I and neutralization buffer on top of one well of a 6-well plate.
Incubate for 1 hour at 37°C.
Check well confluency and organoid condition under the microscope.
Remove ENR medium from wells containing organoids.
Collect Matrigel containing organoids in 250 μl of Cell Recovery Solution.
Pipet mixture vigorously up and down to break apart organoids.
Incubate with TrypLE for 5 min at 37°C if necessary to further break apart organoids.
Transfer the solution to a sterile 15 ml tube and incubate on ice for 30 min to dissolve Matrigel.
Centrifuge at 480×g for 4 min after incubation.
Remove supernatant and proceed with cell pellet.
Add 1 ml of ice-cold PBS if residual Matrigel is visible, then repeat centrifuging steps.
Resuspend pellet in 2 ml organoid medium supplemented with ENR and ROCK inhibitor.
Gently pipette the cell solution on top of the Collagen hydrogel drop by drop.
Pre-warm ENR culture medium.
Aspirate old medium from cells attached and growing on the hydrogels.
Add 2 ml of new ENR culture medium to the cells.
Check confluency under microscope before proceeding with passaging if needed.
Collect the Collagen hydrogels and the 2D grown cells using a 5 ml stripette with 1 ml PBS.
Transfer the mixture in a 15 ml tube for co-culture experiments.
Add 50 μl of Collagenase Type IV to the mixture and place it in an incubator at 37°C for 10 minutes.
After incubation, add 10 ml of PBS at room temperature.
Pipette vigorously to dilute any remaining collagenase.
Centrifuge the solution at 480×g for 4 minutes.
Remove supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in 1 mL ADF medium supplemented with ENR.
Count cells using a cell counting chamber.
Mix equal amounts of two lines (50:50) in an organoid medium supplemented with ENR and ROCK inhibitors to a final volume of 2 mL.
Pipette vigorously to homogenize solution.
Gently pipette mixture on top of a Collagen well.
Optional: Add drug at the desired concentration to the culture medium for co-culture assays with drug treatment.
Refresh the culture medium according to the properties of the added drug.
Perform fluorescent microscopy imaging at predetermined timepoints to analyze cell size and growth in 2D co-cultures.
Optional: Prepare separate wells for different timepoints for flow cytometry analysis of 2D cocultures.
Place the organoid co-culture plate in the imaging system.
Bring the cells into focus.
Choose a focus point for 3D organoid co-cultures by selecting the plane containing most organoids in focus from the z planes of one well.
Keep the same focus for all wells.
Optimize fluorescent intensity of all required channels separately.
Create a scan routine depending on the microscope used.
Scan and save your files.
Set laser intensity settings equal between all conditions and for different timepoints.
Focus on the co-culture using only one color at every timepoint.
Use ImageJ software for image analysis of 2D and 3D co-cultures.
Determine the number and size of organoids in 3D co-cultures using ImageJ.
Measure surface occupation for both 2D and 3D co-cultures using ImageJ.
Split fluorescence channels as part of the image analysis pipeline for Day 1 co-cultures.
Set a thresholding cutoff for distinguishing particles during image analysis.
Measure individual particles to quantify characteristics in the image analysis.
Open ImageJ software.
Import the scanned images.
Split channels for color images.
Set display range for each individual channel.
Adjust brightness and contrast for individual channel.
Set a threshold range in Image → Adjust → Threshold to convert pixels into binary classes.
Use the ‘Default’ threshold algorithm for consistency across all experimental conditions.
Open Analyze → Analyze Particles to analyze particle data.
Label organoid cultures for fluorescence.
Set up gating strategy using samples containing a single fluorophore.
Add DAPI with a final concentration of 10 μM to distinguish living/dead cells before measuring the sample.
Gate the cell population using forward scatter (FSC)-A and side scatter (SSC)-A.
Use FSC-H and FSC-W density plots to exclude doublets.
Gate the DAPI-negative cell population using FSC-H and 405 nanometer (nm) laser with a 450/50 nm bandpass filter.
Detect mCherry+ cells using the 612/23(561) nm laser.
Measure mVenus+ cells using a 530/30(488) nm laser.
Calculate the ratio of mCherry+ to mVenus+ cells.
